title: Scripture and the Holy Spirit
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Scripture and the Holy Spirit teaches that the Spirit of God inspired the written Word and helps believers receive, understand, and obey it. The Holy Spirit never leads God’s people away from Scripture, but works through the Word to glorify Christ and form His people.
summary: Scripture and the Holy Spirit teaches that the Spirit of God inspired the written Word and helps believers receive, understand, and obey it. The Holy Spirit never leads God’s people away from Scripture, but works through the Word to glorify Christ and form His people.
christFocus: The Holy Spirit glorifies Christ through Scripture by revealing His person, work, Gospel, promises, and commands. The Spirit does not draw attention away from Jesus, but leads believers to know, trust, worship, and obey Him through the written Word.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Holy Spirit is the divine author behind Scripture. Human authors wrote real words in real settings, but they did not speak from their own private origin. They were carried along by the Holy Spirit so that the written Word is truly God’s Word.

The Spirit also helps believers receive what God has spoken. Sin darkens understanding, hardens hearts, and resists truth. The Spirit opens eyes, gives understanding, convicts of sin, strengthens faith, and enables believers to receive Scripture as God’s Word.

The Spirit never contradicts Scripture. He does not lead people into private revelations, impressions, experiences, or teachings that overthrow the written Word. The same Spirit who inspired Scripture works in harmony with Scripture.

The Spirit uses the Word as a sword. Through Scripture, He exposes deception, confronts sin, comforts the weak, teaches truth, strengthens prayer, and points believers to Christ. A Spirit-filled life is therefore a Scripture-shaped life.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people separate the Holy Spirit from the Bible, as though spiritual life means moving beyond Scripture. Others read Scripture without dependence on the Spirit, treating the Bible like information to master rather than truth to receive before God.

This doctrine holds both together. Believers need the written Word, and they need the Spirit’s help to rightly receive it. The church becomes unhealthy when it claims the Spirit while ignoring Scripture, or claims Scripture while depending only on human intellect.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Read Scripture with dependence on the Holy Spirit. Pray for understanding, conviction, humility, faith, and obedience. Do not follow any spiritual claim that contradicts God’s Word. Ask the Spirit to use Scripture to lead you closer to Christ, deeper in truth, and stronger in faithful obedience.
